Theorem 4.2. Let M0 be given and let s0 ≥ 0. Assume that v(m)(0) = v0 ∈ ˙H s0 and
suppose further that ∥v(m)(0)∥ ˙H 0 ≤ M0. Let T > 0 and let v(m)(t) be a solution of (4.1)
over [0,T ]. Then v(m)(t) solves (4.10) and, uniformly in m, satisﬁes the estimate
∥v(m)(t)∥ ˙H s0 ≤Ms0 for 0 ≤t ≤T, (4.13)
whereMs0 depends only on M0, T , ∥v(0)∥ ˙H s0 and s0.

Theorem 4.3. Let s0 > 0, v(0) ∈ ˙H s0 and let T > 0 be ﬁxed. Let σ be ﬁxed so that
0 < σ < s0. Then there exists a subsequence of v(m)(t) ( which we still label by (m))
of solutions of (4.1), with the same initial data v(0) ∈ ˙H s0, such that v(m)(t) converges
strongly in Lp([0,T ];H σ), for any ﬁxed 1 < p <∞, and ∗-weakly in L∞([0,T ]; ˙H s0) to
v∞(t); and v∞(t) is a solution of (3.8) in the sense of Deﬁnition 3.1 and is bounded in
L∞([0,T ], ˙H s0) with norm
∥v∞∥L∞([0,T ], ˙H s0 ) ≤Ms0, (4.20)
whereMs0 is as in (4.13). Moreover,
∥v∞(t)∥ ˙H 0 = ∥v0∥ ˙H 0 a.e. in [0,T ]. (4.21)

Theorem 5.1. Let s >1/2, v(0) = v0 ∈ ˙H s, and let T > 0 be ﬁxed. Then the solution
v = v∞ of (3.9), in the sense of Deﬁnition 3.1, which was constructed in Theo rem 4.3
is unique. Moreover, the solution is of the class C([0,T ]; ˙H s), and depends Lipschitz
continuously on the initial data in the sense that is describ ed in (5.18) below. Furthermore,
∥v∞(t)∥ ˙H 0 = ∥v(0)∥ ˙H 0 for all t ∈ [0,T ].

20 REGULARIZATION MECHANISM FOR THE PERIODIC KDV EQUATION

Theorem 6.3. Let s ∈ (0, 1/2] and T > 0. For any initial data v(0) = v0 ∈ ˙H s the
solution v = v∞ of equation (3.9), constructed in Theorem 4.3, is unique on the interval
t ∈ [0,T ], is of the class C([0,T ], ˙H s) and depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial
data in the sense of (6.7).

Theorem 6.4. Let s = 0 and T > 0. For any initial data v(0) = v0 ∈ ˙H 0 the equa-
tion (3.9) has on t ∈ [0,T ] a unique solution of class C([0,T ], ˙H 0), which depends Lipschitz
continuously on the initial data.

Theorem 6.5. Let T > 0 be given, and θ ∈ (−1, 0]. If ∥v0∥ ˙H 0 + ∥w0∥ ˙H 0 ≤M, then the
two solutions v(t) and w(t) of equation (3.9), with v(0) = v0 and w(0) = w0, satisfy the
estimate
∥v −w∥L∞([0,T ], ˙H θ ) ≤C ′C T
M ∥v0 −w0∥ ˙H θ, (6.22)
whereC ′,C M depend only on M and θ.

(i) For sigma>=0, horizon b>0, and ||q||_2<=B0, the Galerkin approximations with nonlinearity projected onto |k|<=m are uniformly bounded in L^infty([0,b];dot H^sigma) by A_sigma depending only on sigma,b,B0,||q||_(dot H^sigma). (ii) If sigma>0 and 0<rho<sigma, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];H^rho), every fixed 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infty dot H^sigma to a coefficientwise integral solution with the same bound and ||y(t)||_2=||q||_2 a.e.. (iii) That solution is unique, is in C([0,b];dot H^sigma), conserves L^2 for every time, and depends Lipschitz continuously on initial data in dot H^sigma: for sigma>1/2 the constant may depend on sigma,b and the two initial dot H^sigma norms; for 0<sigma<=1/2 the continuity and uniqueness assertions hold with the same indicated topology. For sigma=0 there is a unique C([0,b];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation, Lipschitz in its data. (iv) For -1<theta<=0, any two such flows whose initial L^2 norms sum to at most B0 satisfy sup_[0,b]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^b*||y(0)-z(0)||_(dot H^theta). The same norm statements hold for U by the Fourier twist.

For every integer nsrc with 0<=nsrc<Lsrc, put a=t_nsrc=nsrc*tau. In particular nsrc=0 is an admissible step for every tau>0, with a=t_0=0 and t_1=tau. For 0<sigma<=1, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero f,g in H^sigma, the source bilinear stage F_a(t;f,g) satisfies ||F_a(t;f,g)||_(H^beta)<=C*tau^((1+sigma-beta)/(1+sigma-beta0))*||f||_(H^sigma)*||g||_(H^sigma) for every beta in [beta0,1+sigma]. Here beta0=2*sigma-3/2 if 0<sigma<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 if sigma=1/2, and beta0=sigma-1 if 1/2<sigma<=1. Norms in this source assertion are unnormalized; C can depend on sigma and on a fixed epsilon, but not on tau, nsrc, Lsrc or spectral support. The grid horizon Lsrc*tau is auxiliary and need not equal the problem parameter T.
